title: Drinking and drumming with the Prince of Wales
summary: Greer teaches the Prince the Charleston and calls him 'the Wale'.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: is this big magnum of champagne in front of everybody and a bottle of Scotch -- bottle of brandy. One sitting there by me. I look at this fellow, I said, little taste, everything fine so now this cat sitting down on the floor he had one of them brandy snifters, big things, he's going with it. I still don't know who he is. So that goes on, so I say, 'Man, why do you...' (unintelligible)
So anyway, now me and him are buddies. He heard the guys, hey, Sonny -- Duke would say hey, Sonny, play so and so. We're going to play so and so.

So right away he pick up on my name, Sonny, so after awhile, he say, 'I can play the drum.' I say 'Yeah, come on man,' me and him tight now. We're juicing together. 'Go on and play, go ahead.' He say, 'I play the Charleston.' Play, ba, bab, you know, playing. I say 'Yeah, man, that's great.' So then (singing) I showed him how to play it fancy, and he said, 'Man, that's fine, can you show me that.' I say 'anytime,' still guzzling.

Now the people, the women start drifting by and they see this cat drifting by and I see all these women bow to this son of a bitch, curtsy you know, I say this cat must be -- and so the guy -- the waiter come up and say, 'Your Highness, some people want to see you.' You know who he was, the Prince of Wales. I never called him His Highness, he called me Sonny and I'd say, yeah, man, I am talking just like I'm talking to you.
I said, 'oh, you're the Prince of Wales.' He's heir to the throne.

So Wally Simpson from Baltimore, he finally married her, she hated my guts, hated Duke's guts. We were taking up too much attention, so he say, 'I'm leaving now. I got to go say hello to some friends, Sonny, I'll be right back though, don't you go nowhere.' 'I ain't going nowhere, Wale.' Call him the Wale, you know, he's the Prince of Wales, but that's too long, I say Wale, 'I'll be right here Wale when you get back.' He thought that was the cutest thing in the world.

He never forgot it. I called him the Wale. He followed us to Paris, to Scotland. He says, 'Sonny, what's my nickname?' I say 'You're the Wale, man, you're something else.' He thought that the was the greatest thing in the world. He never forgot it. Because we was friends up in Scotland, played a theatre, Sir Harry Lauder was the biggest Scotchman. We met him when he come in the Cotton Club, playing the Wintergarden in New York. He was the biggest thing that ever come out of Scotland. 'You take the high road, and I'll take the low road.' Them kind of people, man.
I look back, man, lady luck rode my shoulder a long time, baby.
